abstract: the graviton self-energy $-i [\mbox{}^{μν} σ^{ρσ}](x;x')$ is the 1pi 2-point function of quantum gravity. it can be used to quantum-correct the linearized einstein equation in order to infer quantum corrections to gravitational radiation and to the force of gravity. as long as the two points are non-coincident, the graviton self-energy does not need regularization at 1-loop order, however, solving the 1-loop effective field equations requires integrating $[\mbox{}^{μν} σ^{ρσ}](x;x')$ over ${x'}^μ$, including ${x'}^μ = x^μ$. to facilitate this we employ dimensional regularization and bphz renormalization to compute the 1-loop contribution to the graviton self-energy, in pure quantum gravity, on de sitter background, in the simplest gauge. we then solve the effective field equations to derive 1-loop corrections to the plane wave mode functions of gravitational radiation, and to the newtonian potential. although it seems possible to renormalize in such a way that the mode function shows no secular growth, the newtonian potential grows like the third power of the number of e-foldings.

title: a singularity theorem for quasi-topological gravities
abstract: quasi-topological theories of gravity have recently attracted substantial attention as several theories in this class have a non-singular black hole as a vacuum and spherically symmetric solution. this motivates the expectation that these theories can provide a resolution to the singularity problem and a description of black holes cores. the known solutions, however, possess a cauchy horizon which denotes the end of predictability of the theory, as the initial data do not determine a unique continuation past this type of horizon. in this paper, we show that penrose singularity theorem can be extended to all the known classes of quasi-topological theories that have non-singular black holes as solutions. we prove that spherical collapse satisfying the null energy condition necessarily leads to future null geodesic incompleteness once a trapped sphere forms. this implies that the lack of predictability of the theories is not an artefact of vacuum solutions and these theories are as problematic as general relativity for the dynamical studies of black hole interiors.

title: static vacuum geometry encodes gravitational collapse and cosmology
abstract: we show that, within covariant hamiltonian gravity in spherical symmetry, a prescribed one-parameter family of static vacuum geometries uniquely determines the local dynamics of gravitational collapse coupled to irrotational dust, despite the nonuniqueness of the underlying gravitational hamiltonian. we further derive necessary and sufficient conditions under which the resulting dynamics admits a homogeneous and isotropic cosmological sector. these conditions establish a two-way correspondence between static vacuum geometries and modified friedmann dynamics and impose a universal restriction on the spatial-curvature dependence of the latter. our results provide a criterion for determining whether independently proposed black-hole and cosmological models can arise from a common covariant gravitational theory.

title: gravitational-wave signal from a short grb relativistic mhd jet
abstract: we analyze the gravitational-wave (gw) signal produced by a relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (mhd) simulation of a short grb jet with parameters corresponding to those of grb 170817a. the signal that is generated in the hidden central engine of the grbs is computed by direct integration of the retarded solution of the linearized einstein equations of an mhd simulation. separating the gw signal into its baryonic and electromagnetic contributions, we identify the physical origin of its dominant features. the waveform is of the memory type, with $h(f) \propto 1/f$ at low frequencies and a knee at $\sim 0.5-0.5$hz set by the energy injection time, which corresponds to the grb duration. a pronounced early peak reflects the opening of the magnetic field lines and the equatorial kick given to the ejecta at the onset of the jet, demonstrating that the gw signal can reveal processes deep in the grb engine that cannot be observed otherwise. the signal is strongest for observers far from the jet axis. the total radiated gw energy is only $\sim 10^{42}$ erg, about $10^{-9}$ of the jet energy; it scales as ${\cal e}^2/τ$ with the shortest variability time $τ$, so this is a lower limit. comparing the predicted spectrum with the sensitivity of current and future detectors, we find that events similar to gw170817 are marginally detectable by decigo from up to 10 mpc and by the einstein telescope from 1 mpc. the injected poynting flux in this simulation was smooth. an engine variable on a millisecond timescale, as predicted in some grb models, would substantially increase the gw energy and detectability.

title: cloudy black-hole configurations of the composed einstein-yang-mills-higgs field theory: analytic treatment
abstract: non-abelian black holes that violate the non-hair conjecture are known to exist in the einstein-yang-mills-higgs field theory. the onset of hair formation in this composed physical system is marked by the presence of `cloudy' black-hole spacetimes, magnetically charged reissner-nordström black holes that support spatially regular linearized field configurations. in the present paper we explore, using {\it analytical} techniques, the physical and mathematical properties of the composed black-hole-linearized-field bound-state configurations of the einstein-yang-mills-higgs theory. in particular, we derive a remarkably compact analytical formula for the discrete resonance spectrum $\{μ_k\}^{k=\infty}_{k=1}$ of the dimensionless mass-radius parameter $μ\equiv m_{\text{w}} r_+$ that characterizes the cloudy black-hole-field configurations in the regime $1\ll r_+\ll m^{-1}_{\text{w}}$ of small-mass weakly-magnetized black holes (here $r_+$ is the horizon radius of the central supporting black hole and $m_{\text{w}}$ is the mass of the yang-mills field due to the higgs effect). interestingly, our results reveal that the excited black-hole-field resonances are characterized by the asymptotic $k$-independent dimensionless ratio ${μ_{k+1}/{μ_{k}}}=e^{-{{2π}/{\sqrt{3}}}}$.

title: first law of thermodynamics for interacting charged black holes and applications
abstract: we derive a mass variation identity expressing the first law of black hole thermodynamics for asymptotically flat, stationary, axisymmetric einstein-maxwell solutions with multiple electrically charged horizons and finite conical axis singularities. under the stated asymptotic and parameter regularity hypotheses, the identity holds for independent variations of all parameters within families of fixed horizon types. on the all-degenerate family, a correction to the adm mass defines a scalar function whose derivatives with respect to angular momenta are the horizon angular velocities. at the majumdar-papapetrou family, its angular momentum hessian is positive definite. combining the first variation identity with a separate theorem on the sign of the conical parameters shows that this hessian is nondecreasing in the positive-semidefinite order along admissible paths of increasing weyl gaps at fixed positive charges.

title: hidden by exponential screening: the invisibility of the dymnikova black hole de sitter core to accretion observables
abstract: the dymnikova spacetime replaces the schwarzschild singularity with a de sitter core, and its lapse deviates from schwarzschild by a factor decaying as $e^{-r^3/(2l_{\rm cr}^2m)}$. whether this screening renders the core invisible to accretion has remained an open quantitative question. we address it with grhd simulations of bhl accretion onto dymnikova bh for six values of the critical length, $0.1m\le l_{\rm cr}\le 1.1m$, the last being 97% of the extremal value. all runs share identical gas parameters and resolution, so any difference in the flow must originate from the geometry. the dynamically relevant quantity is the gravitational acceleration, whose deviation reaches 12% at the inner boundary for the most strongly corrected model, yet the flow responds only locally: the post-shock density drops by 10% in the innermost zone and the quiet-phase accretion rate by 0.12%, with no effect beyond $r\simeq2.7m$. because runs differing by as little as $\sim 10^{-10}$ in the metric decorrelate completely once the shock-cone instability saturates, we compare models statistically using ensembles of independent realizations. the time-averaged accretion rate is then independent of $l_{\rm cr}$ to within 0.8% $(2σ)$ at all radii; the variability amplitude, shock-cone opening angle $(1.077\pm0.003 rad)$, and stagnation radius $(26.8\pm0.3m)$ vary only within the realization scatter; the propagation lags $(75.5\pm1.0m$ and $31.6\pm0.4m)$ agree to within 1.6%; and no power spectrum carries a detectable core signature. accretion onto a dymnikova bh is therefore observationally indistinguishable from accretion onto a schwarzschild black hole: timing observations test the shock-cone mechanism, not the regular core. more broadly, ensemble-based statistical comparisons are essential before differences between simulated accretion flows in different spacetimes can be interpreted as physical.

title: charge-activated birefringence and shadow mimicry around reissner-nordström black holes
abstract: we discover that electric charge can activates birefringence for a neutral vector field coupled to the einstein tensor around a reissner-nordström black hole. changing the electric charge of an uncoupled black hole can mimic one parity's shadow radius of a coupled black hole. the coupling makes the two parity looks differently. it separates their shadow edges of two parities and produces a backward-scattered signal with reversed helicity. however changing the charge alone cannot reproduce both effects. they require both nonzero charge and coupling. at weak coupling, the leading correction is the same for both potential. positive coupling raises the potential, reduces low-frequency absorption and decrease the average shadow radius. negative coupling reverses these trends. the backward signal is nonzero, this is due to the difference between the complex scattering amplitudes of the two parities. it is entirely helicity reversed. for the uncoupled field, the shadows is the same for both parities and the backward intensity vanishes exactly at every charge. we can use the split edge and backward signal to distinguish the coupling from a change of charge alone. a comparison with observations still requires a mechanism that produces and detects this field.

title: spectral instability of charged scalar quasinormal modes and superradiance: stabilizing the unstable
abstract: the spectral instability of black holes has become a central topic of the black-hole spectroscopy program. small changes to the black-hole scattering potential are known to produce disproportionately large migrations of its quasinormal modes in the complex plane, but it is unclear whether this sensitivity carries over to energy extraction through superradiance. we study this relation for massless charged scalar fields on reissner--nordström and reissner--nordström--de sitter backgrounds. a localized positive potential bump, small in mass-scaled height, is displaced outward from the light ring while the original radiative boundary conditions are preserved. in the asymptotically flat case, a quasinormal branch enters the superradiant frequency regime while remaining damped. by searching for competing modes, we show that the least-damped positive-frequency mode also enters this regime, after a series of mode overtakings driven by quasinormal-mode migration. the real-frequency amplification, nevertheless, is only weakly affected and develops no pronounced narrow resonance. in de sitter black holes, the bump can move an initially growing monopole mode into the damped half of the complex plane, stabilizing selected configurations that are initially modally unstable. after stabilization, the peak superradiant amplification can remain above both its unperturbed value and a gain of $100\%$; it falls below $100\%$ only for more distant bump locations. a prescribed positive perturbation can thus suppress modal growth without changing the superradiant frequency bounds or immediately suppressing the scattering peak.

title: integrable mass of kerr-newman-bertotti-robinson black hole
abstract: the nontrivial asymptotic structure of rotating black holes in the bertotti-robinson universe complicates a direct determination of their conserved mass, leading previous studies to rely on a priori thermodynamic input. we address this long-standing problem using integrability methods, establish local analytic existence and uniqueness via the cauchy-kovalevskaja theorem, and obtain a closed expression via a rescaled recurrence whose termination is proved at all orders. the resulting kerr-newman-bertotti-robinson mass coincides with the expression previously derived using the canonical first law identity and reproduces the masses of both kerr-bertotti-robinson subcases. with the mass thus fixed without invoking thermodynamic relations for the first time, we rigorously establish the first law of black-hole thermodynamics and the smarr formula for a whole family of kerr-bertotti-robinson black holes suitable for future applications.

title: exact regular planar black holes solutions in bumblebee gravity
abstract: we discuss possibilities of finding exact regular planar black hole solutions in bumblebee gravity with temporal and radial components of the bumblebee field. we consider quadratic and linear potentials, with vanishing and nonzero cosmological constants, respectively. the field equations determine the nonminimal coupling and the relations between the model parameters. found solution produce regular planar black hole with planar deformation function. analytical expressions for this functions has been found. this solutions free of singularities at the $r=0$.

title: exact static two-body gravitational potential at first self-force order
abstract: the static interaction potential of two non-spinning point masses in general relativity was previously computed through seventh post-newtonian order using methods of effective field theory. its probe limit, or zeroth-self-force contribution, is determined exactly by the schwarzschild geometry. we derive a closed-form expression for the static first-self-force correction, quadratic in the light mass, and establish its weak-field expansion to all orders. working in harmonic gauge, we construct the required green function for the coupled linearised gravitational equations about the schwarzschild background. we fix its homogeneous contributions and regularised coincident limit by matching to the dimensionally continued point-source theory. the result reproduces known perturbative coefficients and determines all higher static post-newtonian coefficients in this mass sector.

title: surrogate model of gravitational waveforms for quasi-circular, spin-aligned, asymmetric-mass black hole binaries based on the hybridization of wasabi-c inspirals with numerical relativity waveforms
abstract: with the incorporation of aligned-spin dynamics into self-force waveform models, such as the wasabi-c inspiral model, and with the release of the sxs collaboration's third public catalog of nr simulations, the gravitational waveform modeling community has made significant advances in the modeling of spinning, asymmetric-mass black hole binaries. in light of these developments, we present wasabinrhybsur2dq15, the first surrogate model to incorporate information from self-force theory, post-newtonian theory, and numerical relativity. the model is trained on 65 hybrid waveforms for quasi-circular, spin-aligned, asymmetric-mass black hole binaries with mass ratios spanning 1:1.25 to 1:20 and aligned-spins for the primary black hole ranging -0.5 to 0.5. the hybrid waveforms are generated from a set of wasabi-c inspirals and nr waveforms from the third sxs public catalog. the model covers the parameter domain $1.25 \leq q \leq 15$ and $|χ_{1z}| \leq 0.5$, and includes the $(2,2),\, (2,1),\, (3,3),\, (4,4),$ and $(5,5)$ spin-weighted spherical harmonic modes. the model also spans the entire ligo-virgo-kagra (lvk) frequency band (with $f_{\text{low}}=20$ hz) for total masses $m \gtrsim 111.5\,m_{\odot}$. we find that the wasabinrhybsur2dq15 model faithfully reproduces the hybrid waveforms with mismatches less than $10^{-3}$ for total masses in the range $80\,m_{\odot} \leq m \leq 300\,m_{\odot}$.

title: tracing source imprints on the gravitational direct wave
abstract: the direct wave component of black hole (bh) ringdown, revealed through quasinormal-mode filters, carries a non-quasinormal-mode imprint of the plunging perturber's dynamics. however, the connection between the source trajectory and the observed direct wave remains incompletely understood. we first show that the full waveform filtered by the frequency-dependent black hole response gives a substantially more localized kernel than the standard rational filter approach. we then show that analytically continuing the teukolsky source variables to complex coordinates allows for a semianalytic direct wave which closely reproduces numerical integration throughout the entire plunge. our generalized steepest-descent method clarifies how coherent emission shapes the imprint of source dynamics on the observed direct wave beyond the light-cone picture.

title: mercury (hg): a relativistic $n$-body simulation for horndeski gravity
abstract: we present mercury, a relativistic $n$-body code for cosmological simulations in the $α$-basis formulation of horndeski gravity. mercury extends a particle-mesh scheme by incorporating the dynamics of the additional scalar degree of freedom and the corresponding modified einstein equations, expressed in terms of the time-dependent functions $α_{\rm k}, α_{\rm b}, α_{\rm m}, α_{\rm t}$ and the effective planck mass $m_*^2$. this generalises our previous implementation of horndeski subclass models, namely $k$-essence and kinetic gravity braiding (kgb), to the general linear horndeski $α$-basis. the code evolves the additional scalar degree of freedom and its effective stress--energy tensor alongside the nonlinear matter and metric fields, so that nonlinear structure formation sources the scalar-field evolution and feeds back on the gravitational potentials. through its interface with hi_class, mercury supports both phenomenological $α$-function parametrisations and covariant horndeski theories; we demonstrate the latter using nkgb, the cubic galileon, and brans--dicke models. we validate the implementation against hi_class in the linear regime and recover the expected nonlinear $k$-essence and kgb limits. for the luminal horndeski models considered here, we show how a running effective planck mass generates gravitational slip through the scalar anisotropic stress and modifies the friction terms governing the vector and tensor metric perturbations. the evolution of $m_*^2$ also modifies the normalisation and scale dependence of the effective dark-energy density contrast, leaving a corresponding imprint on its power spectrum. the present framework provides an intermediate step towards nonlinear horndeski simulations, in which nonlinear scalar self-interactions and screening effects can be incorporated consistently within the same relativistic framework.

title: monge's transport problem in synthetic lorentzian spacetimes
abstract: we prove the existence of solutions to the lorentzian monge problem on synthetic lorentzian spacetimes that satisfy the forward timelike measure contraction property $tmcp^+(k,n)$. the cost for this problem is the time separation function $\ell(x,y)$ (the lorentz distance), which represents the maximum amount a particle can age when traveling from $x$ to $y$. the solution is based on the needle decomposition technique, and amounts to a reduction of the full problem to its one-dimensional counterparts. as an application of needle decomposition, we introduce the blended $tmcp$ condition, and obtain a quantitative refinement of the synthetic hawking singularity theorem. we additionally prove a timelike nonbranching reversibility theorem for $tcd_p(k,n)$ spacetimes, showing that forward $p$-essentially nonbranching spacetimes are backward $p$-essentially nonbranching.

title: symmetries and conservation laws in lie-poisson electrodynamics
abstract: lie-poisson electrodynamics (lpe) is a non-abelian and nonlinear deformation of usual electrodynamics, where the gauge algebra is defined through a lie-algebra-type poisson bracket on space-time. this field-theoretical model arises from noncommutative u(1) gauge theory in the semiclassical limit. we focus on the geometric approach to lpe in the absence of charged matter. we establish a non-trivial field redefinition which, under mild technical assumptions, maps the lpe dynamics to that of maxwell theory. we emphasise that despite the dynamical equivalence, these two theories are not physically equivalent, since the corresponding local gauge-invariant observables are different. we show that our field redefinition is actually a seiberg-witten map between lpe and maxwell theory. using this map, for any symmetry of the maxwell action, we construct generators of lpe symmetries and the corresponding conserved currents. in particular, we obtain deformed poincaré transformations, thereby solving the problem of constructing space-time symmetries in lpe. the deformed symmetries are constructed as active transformations of the gauge field. in the outlook, we propose a natural quantization prescription for lpe based on our field redefinition.

title: upper estimates of the lifespan for the fractional wave equations with time-dependent damping and a power nonlinearity of subcritical and critical fujita exponent
abstract: in this paper, we investigate the cauchy problem of the fractional wave equation with time-dependent damping and the source nonlinearity $f(u)\approx |u|^p$: $$ \begin{cases} \partial_t^2u(t,x)+(-δ)^{σ/2} u(t,x)+b(t) \partial_t u(t,x) =f(u(t,x)),\ &(t,x)\ \in [0,t)\times \mathbb{r}^n,\\ u(0,x)=u_0(x),\ \partial_tu(0,x)=u_1(x),\ &x\ \in\ \mathbb{r}^n, \end{cases} $$ where the damping coefficient behaves as $b(t)\approx (1+t)^{-β}$. we first establish local existence and uniqueness of mild and strong solutions in weighted sobolev spaces by deriving weighted sobolev estimates for the linear propagators and overcoming the spatial-weight coupling in the nonlinearity through the bessel potential estimates. then, in the subcritical and critical cases $1<p\leq p_c:=1+\frac σn$, we derive the upper estimates of the lifespan for the fractional laplacian with $0<σ<2$ and time-dependent damping $β\in [-1, 1)$ via the framework of ordinary differential inequalities. the blow-up results, together with the global existence in the supercritical case obtained in \cite{li}, show that the critical exponent for the fractional wave equation is $p_c=1+\fracσ{n}$ for $0<σ<2$. moreover, combining with the lower estimate of lifespan derived in \cite{li}, we conclude that the estimate in this paper is sharp. note that our result for the critical case is completely new even in the classical case $b(t)=1$. we also consider the case of $β=1$, and obtain the upper estimate of the lifespan.

title: low-regularity global well-posedness for the one-dimensional, defocusing, septic nonlinear schrödinger equation
abstract: in this paper, we show that the one dimensional septic nonlinear schrödinger equation is globally well-posed in $h^s (\mathbb{r})$ when $s > 39/89$ with accompanying polynomial bounds in time. we utilize bilinear estimates to obtain improved bounds on the modified energy increment and prove new $l^{p+3}_{t,x}$ almost morawetz estimates for the defocusing $p$-nls adapted to the low-regularity setting, before specializing to the septic case $p=7$. these tools together allow us to reach sobolev regularities $s<1/2$, showing for the first time a global existence result in the mass supercritical regime for a class of unbounded, discontinuous data.

title: boundary blow-up solutions of second order quasilinear equation on infinite cylinders
abstract: this article studies large solutions, for a class of quasi-linear equations involving p-laplacian on the infinite cylindrical domains. we study the wellposedness of weak large solutions on infinite cylinders by the convergence of large solutions on finite cylinders and observe that any such solution coincides with the large solution on its cross-section. finally, the results are generalized to a class of operators involving non-linearity in the gradient.

title: boundary blowup solutions for the finsler p-laplacian: wellposedness and asymptotic behaviour
abstract: we study the existence of large (boundary blow-up) solutions to semilinear equations involving the finsler p-laplacian on bounded domains with sufficiently smooth boundaries. we establish a keller-osserman-type condition that ensures the existence of such solutions, and show that this condition retains the same integrability as that of the p-laplacian. we examine the influence of the anisotropic norm underlying the finsler p-laplacian on the boundary behaviour of the solution, then derive asymptotic estimates for large solutions near the boundary of the domain. using these boundary asymptotics, we prove uniqueness results for power-type nonlinearities.

title: global well-posedness and uniform long-time control for a class of periodic nls-dysthe equations
abstract: we study a class of periodic nls-dysthe equations of the form $i\partial_tu+a\partial_x^2u+b|u|^2u+i\varepsilon(c\partial_x^3u+d|u|^2\partial_xu+eu^2\partial_x\overline{u})=0$ with $x\in\mathbb t$, $a,b,c,d,e\in\mathbb r$, $abc\neq0$, and $\varepsilon>0$. for $0<\varepsilon\ll1$, equations of this type arise as higher-order modulation models for some nonlinear dispersive pdes, including the klein-gordon equation and the serre-green-naghdi equation modeling the evolution of nonlinear shallow water waves.   we prove local well-posedness in $h^s(\mathbb t)$ for $s>3/2$ for arbitrary admissible coefficients, and establish an $h^1$ continuation criterion for $s\ge2$. under the additional assumption $e\neq0$, a lower-order conservation law provides uniform $h^1$ control and, together with the continuation criterion, yields global well-posedness for $s\ge2$. unlike the previous $h^1$ global theory based on takaoka's periodic well-posedness estimates (2000), our result does not require any non-resonance condition on the coefficients.   our approach relies on the construction of modified higher-order energies, following the strategy developed for the generalized kdv equation by planchon, tzvetkov and visciglia (2023) and for the generalized dnls equation by hayashi, ozawa and visciglia (2025).   motivated by higher-order modulation theory, we exploit the conservation laws of cubic nls and their invariance under the commuting complex mkdv flow to establish sobolev bounds uniform in the modulation parameter $\varepsilon$ on time intervals of order $\varepsilon^{-1}$. this corresponds to physical times of order $\varepsilon^{-3}$, which is the natural time scale anticipated for the nls-dysthe approximation.

title: schrodinger group along the horocycles and egorov's theorem on compact hyperbolic surfaces
abstract: in this paper, we study egorov's theorem for laplacian eigenfunctions on compact hyperbolic surfaces in zelditch's quantization. in this quantization, the remainder in egorov's theorem for eigenfunctions is given explicitly by the second derivatives of the symbols along the weak stable foliation of the geodesic flow. forward in time, we show that egorov's theorem for eigenfunctions is valid to all logarithmic times, far beyond the ehrenfest time t_e=|log h|/2, where h going to 0 is the semiclassical parameter.   backward in time, we introduce the schrodinger group along the stable horocycles, which absorbs the exponentially growing part of the remainder. we show that egorov's theorem for eigenfunctions is valid up to -t_e+t_h for any th going to infinity with 0<=t_h<=t_e. moreover, the limit of the remainder in egorov's theorem at the ehrenfest time -t_e is exactly the difference between the semiclassical measure and the liouville measure, tested against the symbols propagated by the schrodinger group. consequently, egorov's theorem for a sequence of eigenfunctions holds at -t_e (and in fact, at -t_e-t for any fixed t in r if and only if the sequence tends to be equidistributed in the phase space. thus, the quantum unique ergodicity (que) conjecture is equivalent to this egorov property holding for every eigenbasis. furthermore, que holds with a polynomial rate if and only if egorov's theorem holds at -t_e with a polynomial remainder. in this case, egorov's theorem holds beyond -t_e with a polynomial remainder, and the stronger the rate is in que, the longer the time is in egorov's theorem.

title: feynman propagators on exponentially decaying perturbations of stationary spacetimes with compact cauchy surface
abstract: in this paper, we construct feynman propagators on exponentially decaying perturbations of stationary spacetime with compact cauchy surface. the propagators are defined as parametrices of the wave operator on exponentially weighted sobolev spaces defined by complex contours $γ$. we then apply this theory to the computation of indexes of dirac operators using a continuous wick-like rotation to relate it to the riemannian case.

title: weighted fractional commutator estimate and application to the fractional wave equations with time-dependent damping
abstract: in this paper, we first establish a weighted bilinear fractional commutator estimate involving the spatial weight $\langle x \rangle^{2m}$. this estimate provides a powerful tool to resolve the difficulties arising from the nonlocality of the fractional laplacian $(-δ)^{σ/2}$ and the interaction between the unbounded weights and the nonlocal operator at infinity. we then apply this result to investigate the cauchy problem for the fractional wave equation with time-dependent damping and source nonlinearity: $$ \begin{cases} \partial_t^2 u(t,x) + (-δ)^{σ/2} u(t,x) + b(t) \partial_t u(t,x) = |u(t,x)|^p, & (t,x) \in (0,t) \times \mathbb{r}^n, \\ u(0,x) = \varepsilon u_0(x), \quad \partial_t u(0,x) = \varepsilon u_1(x), & x \in \mathbb{r}^n, \end{cases} $$ where $σ\in (0,2)$, the initial data scale with a small parameter $\varepsilon > 0$, and the time-dependent damping coefficient $b(t)$ satisfies $b(t) \approx (1+t)^{-β}$ for $β\in [-1, 1)$. utilizing scaling variables and constructing a weighted energy framework based on theorem 1.1, we derive a priori differential inequalities for the total energy. for the supercritical case $p > p_c := 1 + \fracσ{n}$, we prove the small-data global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions in weighted sobolev spaces $h^{σ/2,m}(\mathbb{r}^n) \times h^{0,m}(\mathbb{r}^n)$ by closing a bootstrap argument. for the subcritical ($1 < p < p_c$) and critical ($p = p_c$) cases, we establish precise lower bounds for the lifespan $t_\varepsilon$ of blow-up solutions via delicate ode analysis. together with the corresponding upper estimates, our results fully determine the sharp lifespan estimates for all $β\in [-1, 1)$, confirming that $p_c = 1 + \fracσ{n}$ is indeed the critical exponent for the fractional wave equation with time-dependent damping.

title: spectral analysis and shape optimization of steklov--dirichlet eigenvalues on shell-type domains
abstract: we investigate the steklov--dirichlet eigenvalues on shell-type domains in $\mathbb{r}^n$, $n\geq 2$, where the steklov and dirichlet conditions are imposed on the outer and the inner boundaries, respectively. we introduce the green function associated with the problem, which is well-defined for spectral parameters outside the spectrum and exhibits blow-up behavior at eigenvalues, and establish its spectral representation. we also examine its differentiability and derive its shape derivative under translations of the inner boundary. using these results and a layer potential approach, we propose a computational framework for optimizing the eigenvalue with respect to the position of the inner boundary, incorporating an eigenvalue estimator for which a local error bound is established. numerical experiments for various inner and outer boundary shapes demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in identifying configurations that maximize the first eigenvalue.

title: uniqueness in an incompressible fluid with objective heat conduction model
abstract: in the context of heat conduction, the equations of maxwell-cattaneo is a successful alternative to the fourier's law. in 2009, christov proposed a frame-independent (or objective) generalization of maxwell-cattaneo equation. for a more general class of objective heat conduction maxwell-cattaneo-christov equations proposed by angeles, a uniqueness result is proved, applied to an incompressible fluid.

title: boundary determination from the anisotropic elastic dirichlet-to-neumann map
abstract: we show that the dirichlet-to-neumann map of the elastic wave equation determines the density and the anisotropic stiffness tensor on the boundary for generic density and stiffness tensor fields. the proof builds on an interplay between microlocal analysis and algebraic geometry. microlocal analysis yields a construction of special solutions, valid for many real principal type systems, that concentrate near a boundary point. generic conditions ensure that this construction holds and allow for extraction of information about stiffness tensor and density at the boundary. we also describe the generic sets through algebraic conditions.

title: the landau equation: well-posedness and singularities of homoenergetic solutions
abstract: we consider the inhomogeneous landau equation and focus on solutions whose density and temperature evolve in time but remain spatially homogeneous. such solutions are called homoenergetic. we identify one class of initial data for which homoenergetic solutions exist globally in time, and another class for which they develop finite-time hydrodynamic singularities. the initial data are spatially inhomogeneous, neither close to vacuum nor close to equilibrium; both the well-posedness and the finite-time blow-up results hold for all soft and hard potentials.

title: modulational stability of finite-depth stokes waves with constant vorticity
abstract: we investigate the effect of constant vorticity on the modulational spectral stability of small-amplitude periodic gravity waves for the two-dimensional finite-depth water-wave system. we derive an explicit stability criterion that agrees with the prediction obtained by thomas, kharif and manna [43] through a nonlinear schrödinger approximation. for waves propagating to the right, we identify a sharp range of dimensionless positive (counterclockwise) vorticity, for which modulational instability is suppressed at every depth, while at any fixed depth sufficiently strong negative (clockwise) vorticity also restores modulational stability. we give a complete description of the spectrum near the origin and identify a figure-eight spectral curve in the unstable regime. a key distinction from the irrotational case is that the usual hamiltonian factorization of the linearized operator fails at zero floquet exponent on the full periodic sobolev space. we therefore carry out a spectral reduction based on reversibility, without relying on hamiltonian factorization.

title: anisotropic minkowski flows: well-posedness and asymptotic behaviour
abstract: we study anisotropic minkowski-type curvature flows associated with a perimeter defined through oscillations on wulff neighbourhoods. the anisotropy may be non-smooth, and in particular crystalline, while the mobility may differ from the anisotropy, provided a natural compatibility condition is satisfied. we compute the first variation of the perimeter and introduce a weak formulation in terms of distance functions and measure-valued nonlocal cahn-hoffman fields. by means of a nonlocal minimising movement scheme and suitable estimates for the evolution of wulff shapes, we prove existence of weak superflows and subflows starting from arbitrary closed sets. under the additional assumption that the initial level sets have compact boundary, a comparison principle yields existence and uniqueness of the level set flow. finally, we prove that variational weak flows converge, up to fattening, as $r\searrow 0$ to the weak flow of the local anisotropic, possibly crystalline, curvature motion. the main step in the proof consists in averaging the nonlocal cahn-hoffman measures to obtain vector fields converging to a local cahn-hoffman field.

title: global existence for a drift-diffusion model of electrical discharge in mems
abstract: we study a coupled elliptic-parabolic system modelling electrical discharge in a micro-electro-mechanical (mems) capacitor: a poisson equation for the electrostatic potential, coupled to drift-diffusion equations for the ion and electron densities with a townsend ionization source whose rate per electron grows linearly in the electric field. gimperlein, he and lacey proved local well-posedness and left open whether the densities blow up in finite time. we first prove a continuation criterion in a weak norm: a finite-time singularity forces the space charge to be unbounded in h^1_d, the dual of the space of h^1 functions vanishing on the electrodes, so blow-up cannot be quasi-neutral. we then exclude it altogether when the two diffusivities coincide and the vacuum field is bounded: the weak solution is then global in time. to our knowledge this is the first global existence result without smallness assumptions for a drift-diffusion-poisson model of gas discharge whose ionization rate is unbounded in the field. the proof uses the electrostatic energy and the number of carriers in place of the usual free energy: the ionization source cancels in the energy balance, the joule heating is dissipative, and the two quantities close through a linear gronwall inequality. numerical experiments on a discharge in a micrometre gap, with the townsend constants and the mobilities of air, provide evidence for the extension to unequal diffusivities and bear on the existence of a breakdown threshold.

title: uniform local smoothing for the derivative nls and the soliton mass threshold
abstract: harrop-griffiths, killip, ntekoume and vişan proved that the derivative nonlinear schrödinger equation (dnls) is globally well-posed in $l^2(\mathbb{r})$. a key ingredient of their proof is a local smoothing estimate. it holds on $l^2$-equicontinuous sets of initial data, but it cannot hold on $l^2$-balls, because rescaled stationary solitons, all of mass $2π$, violate it. this raises a natural question: for which masses $m$ does local smoothing hold uniformly on the ball $\{m(q_0)\le m\}$? we prove three results. first, we give a quantitative version of the local smoothing estimate in which the data enter only through the mass and an explicit frequency scale $κ(q_0)$. on time intervals of length $2t$ the bound grows like $1+κ(q_0)^2t$, and the stationary soliton shows that the power of $κ$ cannot be lowered below one. second, we prove uniform local smoothing on balls of small mass, together with a scale-invariant morrey-type form and a localized $l^4_{t,x}$ bound. third, we analyse the soliton family from both sides. the uniform constant must blow up at least like $(2π-m)^{-1}$ as $m\uparrow 2π$, while every soliton of mass $m<2π$ satisfies local smoothing with a constant $o((2π-m)^{-1})$. these facts single out the stationary-soliton mass $2π$, which is also the hayashi--ozawa coercivity threshold, as the natural candidate for the sharp threshold. we formulate this as a conjecture, give a spectral reformulation in terms of the kaup--newell scattering data, and discuss the obstacles to a proof.

title: einstein-non-linear maxwell-yukawa black hole
abstract: within the context of nonlinear electromagnetism, we consider the yukawa extension of a reissner-nordström black hole. an exact solution is given which modifies certain characteristics of the latter. some thermodynamical aspects are given for comparison. the model provides a gauge-invariant nonlinear-electrodynamic realization of a screened electric potential; the yukawa form by itself does not establish a massive vector excitation. the exact spacetime solution and its thermodynamic properties are examined with the exponential-integral contribution.

title: universality of primordial anisotropies in gravitational wave background
abstract: we investigate the general structure of primordial anisotropies in the stochastic gravitational-wave background (sgwb). many mechanisms generating primordial sgwb anisotropies, including fossil and propagation effects, exhibit similar multipole dependences despite their distinct physical origins, implying the presence of a common underlying structure. to characterize this structure, we introduce a model-independent framework, the cosmological form factor (cff), that describes how long-wavelength perturbations modulate short-scale sgwb statistics. within this broad class of mechanisms, we show that the allowed angular and polarization structures of sgwb anisotropies are universally determined by general principles, including statistical isotropy, locality, and the basic properties of long-wavelength perturbations. in contrast to these universal structures, observables such as amplitudes and frequency dependence retain information about the origin. our results provide a unified and effective description of primordial sgwb anisotropies, clarifying which aspects are universal and which are model dependent, and therefore offer a theoretical foundation for interpreting future gravitational-wave observations.

title: dark graviton sensing with magnetically levitated superconductors
abstract: levitated sensors have emerged as a new frontier to detect ultra-light dark matter such as axion-like particles and dark photons. in this work we study how a magnetically levitated superconductor responds to a spin-2 dark matter field, the dark graviton, in the dhz to khz frequency range. to do so, we compute the forces that the dark graviton exerts on the superconductor, separately for matter and light couplings. the matter coupling produces a strain-like tidal acceleration between the superconductor and the centre of mass of the rigid apparatus, resulting in a displacement relative to the readout pick-up loop, in a way analogous to the response to a slow, continuous, massive gravitational wave. the light coupling instead induces an effective current that sources an oscillating magnetic field, thus driving the superdiamagnetic response of the superconductor. we find that, albeit with significant experimental improvements, the sensitivity reach for the matter coupling could surpass existing fifth-force experiments in the audio frequency band. at the same time, magnetically levitated superconductors could be among the most sensitive laboratory probes of the dark-graviton coupling to electromagnetism, especially at low frequencies, provided technical and readout noise can be kept under control.

title: photon propagation and black hole imaging in kruglov nonlinear electrodynamics
abstract: nonlinear electrodynamics (nled) modifies photon propagation through an effective optical geometry, allowing optical phenomena to deviate from those predicted solely by the underlying spacetime metric. in this work, we revisit the kruglov model, which generalizes born--infeld electrodynamics, and investigate the corresponding null geodesics in theeffective geometry through direct numerical integration, without relying on strong-field analytical approximations. we analyze the resulting photon spheres, gravitational lensing, black-hole shadows, and thin accretion-disk images, together with their dependence on the parameter $q$. for sufficiently small positive $q$, the effective angular metric develops a pole that generates stable photon orbits outside the event horizon and locally reverses the azimuthal evolution of photon trajectories, producing a distinctive bending pattern that resembles, although does not originate from, frame dragging. conversely, negative $q$ introduces a zero of the effective correction factor, which acts as a turning point for photon trajectories and prevents them from entering the region where the background metric becomes complex. it produces measurable changes in light deflection, shadow radius, photon-ring morphology, and relativistic images. in particular, smaller positive values of $q$ produce thinner photon rings and enlarged shadow radii, whereas negative values generally lead to broader photon rings and smaller shadows. comparison with the current event horizon telescope constraints on sgr~a* shows that a substantial region of the kruglov parameter space remains compatible with present observations.

title: parity-dependent wave absorption and optical characteristics of a cored magnetic black hole
abstract: we study light propagation and coupled gravitational--electromagnetic waves around a black hole supported by a nonlinear magnetic field. the same field action fixes the geometry, the mass--charge relation, and the wave potentials. we calculate two critical impact parameters for light and solve the coupled scattering equations in both parity sectors. in eight solutions of one action, the two optical scales differ by $3.6$--$7.2\%$. the wave absorption also depends on parity. for $\ell=2$, the gap between the larger absorption eigenvalues reaches about $9.0$ percentage points. a wider frequency scan reveals a stronger effect in the second eigenchannel. the difference between the two absorption traces reaches $24.3$ percentage points. the trace equals twice the absorption of an equal incoherent mixture of incoming gravitational and electromagnetic fields. a controlled test of the wave operator shows that the nonlinear electromagnetic factor $κ$ plays an important role in the parity gap. we also examine four $\ell=3$ cases and use charge-matched reissner--nordström black holes as a separate control. the optical and wave calculations provide two complementary properties of the same magnetic source.

title: opening the window of ultra-light pbhs by exorcising the poltergeist
abstract: the hot big bang may have emerged from evaporation of primordial black holes (pbhs) lighter than $10^9$g. standard monochromatic treatments predict nearly simultaneous evaporation, abrupt reheating, and a large poltergeist scalar-induced gravitational wave signal. we confront this expectation with the irreducible collapse mass tail predicted by general relativity, $df_{\rm pbh}/d\ln m\propto m^{3.78}$, which smooths reheating, suppresses the signal by orders of magnitude, and reopens the ultra-light pbh window.

title: perturbative dynamics and relativistic effects of a dyonic kalb-ramond black hole
abstract: we investigate perturbative dynamics, tidal effects, and relativistic frequency shifts in a dyonic kalb-ramond black hole generated by a lorentz-violating antisymmetric tensor background. the geometry is controlled by the mass $m$, the electric charge $q$, the magnetic charge $p$, and the lorentz-violating parameter $\ell$, with the dyonic sector entering through the effective combination $p_{\ell}^{2}=q^{2}/(1-\ell)^{2}+p^{2}/(1-2\ell)$. first, we analyze the gravitational doppler effect for radial signal exchange between freely falling and static observers, showing how the dyonic charges weaken the redshift by shifting the frequency ratio toward unity. we then compute the radial and angular tidal forces in a freely falling frame and determine the characteristic radii at which the usual stretching and compression patterns are reversed. the gravitational time delay is also evaluated for null trajectories, showing that the electric and magnetic sectors reduce the delay relative to the reference configuration. in the perturbative sector, we study massless scalar, vector, and spinor test fields together with an effective axial metric model, computing sixth-order wkb spectra and independently checking selected modes using the asymptotic iteration method. at fixed mass and charges, increasing the lorentz-violating parameter raises the tabulated oscillation frequencies and damping rates in the original time coordinate; their interpretation accounts for time normalization and changes in effective parameters. the independent comparisons support the tested higher-multipole fundamental modes. time-domain evolutions exhibit damped ringdown followed by power-law tails, whose exponents are estimated through fits incorporating finite time corrections and numerical sensitivity checks.

title: odd-parity ringdown gravitational waves of a spherically symmetric black hole with perfect fluid accretion
abstract: the ringdown waves from a black hole offer a clean probe of strong-field gravity, but a matter distribution that may be present around a realistic black hole renders the background spacetime dynamical and the ringdown frequencies time-dependent. we study the odd-parity ringdown of a schwarzschild black hole that grows through the dilute, steady, spherically symmetric accretion of a perfect fluid. working to first order in the accretion rate, we compute the ringdown waveform directly in the time domain on this dynamical background. since the odd-parity matter perturbation decouples from the metric perturbation, the wave mode can be described by a purely tensorial mode on the accreting background. in particular, the ratio of the imaginary to the real part of the frequency cancels both the secular variation caused by the growth of the black hole and the redshift factor, so that its deviation from the schwarzschild value purely reflects the surrounding environment. the time dependence of the frequency, on the other hand, reflects the accretion rate and allows us to define a second observable tied to it. we argue that measuring these observables across multiple modes may provide significant information to constrain the surrounding environment of the black hole.

title: universal bounds on black hole observables imposed by energy conditions
abstract: energy conditions (ecs) underpin fundamental results in general relativity, yet their observational validity in strong gravitational fields remains largely untested. here, we establish a direct correspondence between the local stress-energy tensor, photon-orbit dynamics, and strong-field observables associated with black hole shadows, photon rings, and eikonal gravitational-wave ringdown for static, spherically symmetric black holes within general relativity. we show that imposing local ecs at unstable photon spheres yields analytic bounds on these observables. in particular, the demagnification of successive photon rings provides an exact diagnostic of the local tangential null energy condition. these bounds offer a direct route to constraining the matter fields sourcing spacetimes and testing ecs through strong-field observations. combining them with observational measurements of these observables further restricts admissible black hole geometries and additionally constrains the otherwise inaccessible photon sphere geometry and local stress-energy content, demonstrating their observational potential in the strong-field regime.

title: multipolar neutrino radiation in binary neutron star mergers: angular structure, rotational variability, and implications for electron fraction
abstract: the angular structure and temporal variability of neutrino emission from binary neutron star mergers are characterized using fully general-relativistic simulations with energy-integrated m1 neutrino transport across a representative set of equations of state, total masses and mass ratios. the main analysis is restricted to merger remnants that do not collapse to a black hole within the simulated time intervals. the angle-dependent neutrino energy flux is extracted on a spherical surface outside the remnant and decomposed into spherical harmonics to quantify its multipolar content and evolution. following the initial post-merger transient, the neutrino radiation flux approaches an axisymmetric configuration dominated by a strong quadrupolar component, producing persistent polar flux enhancement and equatorial suppression due to torus shadowing. the dipolar contribution remains subdominant, indicating the absence of sustained one-sided emission. the degree of anisotropy increases with mass asymmetry and for softer equations of state, reflecting the compactness and morphology of the remnant--disk system. superimposed on this time-averaged geometry, coherent azimuthal modulations associated with the $m=1$ mode are identified. the associated half frequency, $f_{\mathrm{dom}}/2\simeq0.6$--$0.7\,\mathrm{khz}$, is compared with local rotation rates in the simulated remnant--disk systems, suggesting a possible dynamical association between the remnant structure and neutrino variability. finally, we quantify how the same quadrupole-dominated radiation geometry induces a latitude-dependent equilibrium electron fraction. the polar material is driven close to the neutrino-equilibrium target, whereas equatorial material remains systematically more neutron rich and below equilibrium.

title: non-stationary wormholes and matter source reconstruction in general relativity
abstract: we investigate non-stationary wormhole geometries in general relativity embedded in evolving cosmological backgrounds. we employ a simpson-visser-like regularization of the temporal coordinate of the $(n+1)$-dimensional flrw metric, together with a homogeneous cuscuton field, to construct cosmological backgrounds in which the scale factor remains finite and non-zero at the would-be initial singularity. we then consider two specific dynamical wormhole geometries: the four-dimensional defect wormhole and the topologically charged perry-mann type wormhole. we show that the former can be supported by a canonical scalar field with vanishing potential, while the latter requires a mimetic matter sector to support its spatial structure, with the cuscuton governing the cosmological evolution in both cases. we subsequently generalize the analysis to a separable non-stationary spacetime and derive a scaling condition that strongly constrains the admissible matter sources. in particular, for minimally coupled scalar and nonlinear electrodynamics fields, this condition removes the functional freedom available in static reconstruction schemes. we show that, within this framework, regular, asymptotically flat wormhole geometries cannot be obtained while simultaneously satisfying the required smoothness and reflection symmetry conditions. our results illustrate both the possibility of constructing specific non-stationary wormholes in regular cosmological backgrounds and the restrictions that arise when attempting to generalize such constructions to arbitrary spatial geometries.

title: gauge-invariant non-universal scalar couplings in teleparallel gravity
abstract: we develop a gauge-invariant teleparallel framework in which the universality of the gravitational coupling is relaxed for a scalar field, while the gravitational sector retains the form of the teleparallel equivalent of general relativity. the non-universal interaction is encoded in a scalar-sector tetrad whose coupling to the universal translational gauge potential is controlled by a field-dependent gravitational charge. a stückelberg completion preserves local translational gauge invariance, and we derive the gravitational, scalar-field, and stückelberg equations, together with the antisymmetric constraint and their consistency relations. as a first application, we investigate homogeneous and isotropic cosmology, where the stückelberg constraint provides a first integral governing the evolution of the non-universal coupling. in the kination-dominated regime, the standard stiff-fluid behavior is recovered asymptotically, whereas in the potential-dominated regime, accelerated expansion requires additional conditions beyond potential domination. we identify compatible expanding solutions in which departures from universality are dynamically suppressed, including examples approaching power-law inflation or asymptotically de sitter expansion. including a universally coupled perfect fluid and a constant scalar potential, we obtain a late-time solution exhibiting a subdominant matter-like contribution to the background friedmann equation and an asymptotic de sitter limit. these results provide a gauge-theoretic realization of non-universal scalar couplings and highlight their potential implications for early- and late-time cosmology.

title: reference-renormalized jacobi primitives for finite-distance massive-particle deflection
abstract: we develop a reference-renormalized jacobi-primitive gauss-bonnet formalism for finite-distance weak deflection of massive particles in static, spherically symmetric spacetimes. the construction uses the fixed-energy jacobi metric associated with timelike geodesics and treats the radial curvature primitive as a quantity defined only up to an additive constant. instead of fixing this constant by requiring the primitive to vanish at a circular timelike orbit, we subtract a reference jacobi geometry at the same conserved particle energy and impose endpoint normalization on the curvature-density discrepancy. this gives a circular-orbit-free primitive representation of the gauss-bonnet curvature contribution while preserving the operational finite-distance definition of the bending angle through local source and receiver directions. we prove that the reference-normalized and circular-orbit-normalized prescriptions agree whenever both are admissible, since their primitives differ only by a constant that cancels from the exact curvature strip integral. the method remains applicable when no admissible circular timelike orbit exists, when the orbit lies outside the riemannian jacobi domain, or when the natural no-lens comparison geometry is non-euclidean. we demonstrate the formalism in three representative settings: schwarzschild-like bumblebee, kottler, and janis-newman-winicour (jnw) spacetimes. the formalism therefore identifies circular-orbit anchoring as an auxiliary primitive gauge choice rather than a prerequisite for finite-distance jacobi gauss-bonnet deflection.

title: nonexistence of multiple black holes in stationary analytic vacuum spacetimes
abstract: we prove the nonexistence of non-rotating and degenerate horizon components in the stationary, asymptotically flat, $i^+$-regular, analytic vacuum spacetime. this result rules out the final case in the classification of stationary analytic black-hole spacetimes. consequently, the stationary, asymptotically flat, $i^+$-regular, analytic vacuum black hole uniqueness conjecture is settled affirmatively in full.

title: bouncing and qnm convergence in kerr
abstract: we show that the convergence region of the qnm representation of the retarded green's function of the kerr spacetime is set by complex-time bouncing singularities, as in our previous work for the schwarzschild case. the main difference between kerr and schwarzschild is that there are two distinct qnm families, prolate and oblate, which have different convergence regions. we provide explicit analytical formulae for the bounce radii and corresponding convergence regions in boyer-lindquist coordinates. we also provide an analysis of convergence in the reissner-nordström spacetime.

title: multi-domain spectral method for kerr spacetimes: a hyperboloidal teukolsky $m$-mode solver for self-force computations
abstract: we solve the frequency-domain, $m$-mode teukolsky equation for the spin-weight $s=-2$ weyl scalar $ψ_4$ sourced by a point mass on a circular, equatorial orbit around a kerr black hole. the equation is posed on hyperboloidal slices that reach the event horizon and future null infinity, so that the physical (retarded) solution is selected by regularity alone, without imposing radiation conditions. the particle is treated with the $m$-mode puncture/effective-source scheme, and the resulting two-dimensional elliptic problem is solved with a four-domain pseudo-spectral method in which the equatorial symmetry is broken and handled by an even/odd decomposition of the field. we test the method for orbital radius $r_0=10m$ and spins up to $|a|/m=0.9$, covering prograde and retrograde orbits. the energy fluxes to infinity agree with independent black hole perturbation toolkit results to $\sim10^{-7}$ for the dominant modes and to better than $2\times10^{-5}$ for all modes up to $m=20$ at moderate resolutions. the static $m=0$ mode requires no special treatment.

title: kerr metric perturbations for second-order self-force theory
abstract: we present a calculation of the first-order metric perturbation arising from a point mass moving on a circular, equatorial orbit in kerr spacetime. the metric perturbation is specifically aimed at meeting the requirements of second-order self-force theory: it is highly accurate; incorporates all contributions, including those associated with perturbations to the black hole's mass and angular momentum; is in lorenz gauge near the worldline and in (near) bondi--sachs gauge at large radius; and can be efficiently evaluated across the entire exterior spacetime. the lorenz gauge gives a well-understood singular structure at the particle, while the (near) bondi--sachs gauge ensures the asymptotic fall-off needed for an asymptotically flat second-order source. our formalism reconstructs the metric from separable teukolsky-type equations, decomposed into spin-weighted spheroidal harmonic modes and solved spectrally on hyperboloidal slices. the resulting $(\ell,m)$-mode sums converge rapidly across most of the domain, but slowly near the point mass; we overcome this with a novel use of a puncture to extract accurate $m$-mode data, yielding output accurate to $\sim 10^{-10}$ per $m$-mode and suitable for use at second order. our metric-perturbation results cover a range of kerr spins $-0.9 \le a/m \le 0.9$ and orbital radii out to $50m$. in addition to its immediate application in second-order self-force calculations, our results can also be used as input to other calculations involving kerr metric perturbations, including studies of environmental effects and quasinormal modes.

title: noisy pipelines ii: non-parametric noise inference for lisa
abstract: the laser interferometer space antenna (lisa) is expected to observe gravitational-wave signals from massive black hole binaries, extreme mass ratio inspirals, and more. despite the significant scientific potential, accurately extracting these signals from the data will only be possible if lisa's instrumental noise is understood: poor noise modelling will result in lost signals, biased parameter estimates, and incorrect astrophysical insights. modelling lisa's instrumental noise is more challenging than its ground-based counterpart since the data is highly correlated, meaning that the noise covariance matrix can no longer be assumed diagonal in frequency and in the different data streams. in this work, we present an initial approach to perform non-parametric noise inference for lisa that requires no prior knowledge of the lisa observatory. by fitting the full noise covariance matrix with a combination of splines and inverse lorentzians, we show that our model can estimate the power and cross spectral densities for lisa from 7 days of simulated noise-only data. we find that the median estimate from our non-parametric model whitens the data according to the expected unit normal distribution. we envision that our non-parametric model can be used as part of the global fit, as well as in combination with modelled approaches to identify, quantify, and constrain the frequency dependence of unknown noise artifacts.

title: binary black hole mergers in massive einstein-scalar-gauss-bonnet gravity
abstract: we study fully non-linear binary black hole mergers in massive einstein-scalar-gauss-bonnet (esgb) gravity with a linear gauss-bonnet coupling function. in the absence of a well-developed initial data solver for esgb gravity, we demonstrate that the conventional workaround solution for massless scalar fields results in confined junk radiation that contaminates late-time dynamics in the massive theory. we propose a solution to this problem by suitably modifying the equations of motion at the early stages of the simulation to tame such junk radiation, thereby allowing us to study the dynamics of the scalar field during the process of a black hole merger. this is followed by a preliminary analysis of the frequency content in the ringdown of the scalar and tensor modes. in particular, the quadrupole scalar mode exhibits a rich ringdown structure: while it is dominated by the spin-2 ``contamination'' frequency in the early stages, its late time morphology becomes primarily determined by the scalar mass frequency.

title: quasi-normal modes and instabilities of rotating relativistic stars
abstract: we derive the basic equations suitable for the coupled fluid--spacetime eigenvalue problem from the second-order action in full general relativity and accurately determine quasi-normal modes of a variety of rapidly rotating stars with outgoing-wave boundary conditions. for mit-bag strange stars, the spectrum realizes chandrasekhar's instability picture, with distinct chandrasekhar--friedman--schutz and jacobi-like neutral conditions and the transition to dynamical bar-mode growth. for neutron stars, we determine the $f$-, $r$-, and other inertial-mode spectra and their radiative damping or growth times. interactions between $f$- and inertial modes reveal avoided crossings and exchanges for radiative damping or growth rates. we locate quasiradial collapse thresholds through a static stability analysis and independently verify them by tracking the fundamental $f$-mode frequency to zero, clarifying that the central density at the onset of the dynamical instability is always larger than that of the secular instability for uniform rotation. our formalism and numerical implementation can also resolve highly damped $w$-modes.

title: multimessenger astrophysics drives the case for an australian gravitational-wave observatory
abstract: the next generation of an international network of gravitational-wave observatories is now in the advanced planning stages. with australia's substantial history of contributions in this field, its history of scientific mega-projects like the square kilometer array, and its unique geographic location and conditions, it is ideally placed to host an observatory in the global network. it has already been demonstrated that a gravitational wave detector in australia plays an important role in minimizing the sky localization uncertainty of gravitational wave events. we study a particular science case for an australian observatory, focusing on its potential contributions to multimessenger astronomy. we demonstrate that an observatory in australia can enable the detection of up to eight multimessenger gravitational-wave plus kilonova events per year, with localisations better than $1-10°^2$ in both second- and third-generation networks. we show that, in a global network of xg observatories, an australian observatory with 2g sensitivity would still enable significant advances in multimessenger science. the full case for an australian observatory must be considered in a much broader context; however, this work indicates it could make substantial contributions to multimessenger astrophysics.

title: how fast do black holes spin?
abstract: we present a systematic study of the spin evolution of accreting black holes. using the bhac code for general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations, we conduct a total of 500 high resolution simulations of magnetized accretion disks around kerr bhs with spin parameters ranging from $χ=0$ to $χ= 0.99$. the baseline configuration follows the default fishbone--moncrief torus setup in bhac. we further explore the effects of: i) introducing multiple poloidal magnetic loops, ii) the initial position of the torus, iii) magnetic field strength and iv) radial loop modulation. from each simulation we extract the mass flux and angular momentum flux through the horizon to compute the time-averaged spin evolution rate after the system becomes quasi-stationary. the equilibrium spin ranges from $χ_{\rm eq}\simeq0.88$ in the fiducial model to $χ_{\rm eq}\simeq0.98$ for weak-flux model. applied to sgr a$^*$, even an optimistic estimate for rapid spin evolution gives a timescale longer than $10^{13}$ yr, indicating an earlier growth or merger history. these trends are consistent with the picture that larger net magnetic flux threading the horizon enhances jet-torques and reduces the equilibrium spins, whereas weak net flux yields near-maximal spins. our results provide a pathway to interpret the high spins reported for x-ray binaries and active galactic nuclei and they sharpen the astrophysical viability of near-horizon high-energy processes that rely on near-extremal black holes.

title: imaginary time as a complex representation of relativity
abstract: we develop a systematic complex representation of lorentzian relativity based on the imaginary temporal coordinate $x^0=ict$. rather than treating this substitution as a wick rotation to euclidean spacetime, we formulate it as an invertible change of representation in which physical spacetime is identified with a real subspace of a complex vector space. this construction introduces two related metric structures: a complex-bilinear form and a hermitian form, both of which reproduce the original lorentzian interval when restricted to physical spacetime. we extend the representation to relativistic dynamics, including proper time, four-momentum, and the hamilton-jacobi formulation, and show that the metric, connection, curvature tensors, einstein equations, and conservation laws retain their conventional content in curved spacetime. explicit applications to the kerr and friedmann-lemaître-robertson-walker geometries demonstrate consistency for rotating and time-dependent spacetimes. we further examine relativistic wave equations and their nonrelativistic limit, showing how the schrödinger equation and its relation to euclidean-time evolution emerge within the same complex temporal framework. the resulting formulation introduces no new physical predictions, but clarifies the geometric role of imaginary temporal coordinates and reveals structural connections among relativistic geometry, action, wave propagation, and analytic continuation.

title: late-time echoes from planar wave-packet scattering by an ultracompact star
abstract: we simulate the propagation and scattering of an incident plane scalar wave in the spacetime of an ultracompact, horizonless constant-density star using a time-domain multipole mode-sum method. by reconstructing the coherently superposed time-domain waveforms, we compare the star's dynamical response with that of a schwarzschild black hole. we find that the early-time response closely mimics a black-hole ringdown due to wave scattering near the exterior unstable photon sphere. conversely, the late-time signal develops a sequence of delayed echoes originating from wave trapping near the interior stable light ring and subsequent leakage through the exterior potential barrier. while individual multipoles exhibit regular echoes, their coherent superposition induces interference, producing complex waveforms with irregular profiles that nonetheless retain an underlying temporal organization with alternating peak separations. finally, as a proof of concept, we perform a signal-to-noise ratio analysis using an assumed strain normalization, demonstrating that these weak, late-time signatures can be resolved by third-generation gravitational-wave detectors.

title: on mass inflation and late-time divergences in limiting-curvature regular black holes
abstract: mass inflation in non-extremal regular black holes with a non-linear dependence of the misner-sharp mass $m$ on the asymptotic mass $m>0$ may be a transient phenomenon followed by a model-dependent non-exponential late-time divergence. we analyse these regimes based on the generalised ori model for a class of static spherically symmetric and asymptotically flat regular black holes with a de sitter core and an $m$-independent upper bound on the misner-sharp mass density and kretschmann scalar inspired by quasi-topological gravity. we discuss the geometric mechanism behind divergences of physical quantities at the inner horizon of the perturbed spacetime, and show that these require the unphysical mass parameter inside the shell to evolve outside the positive-real domain, or in some cases force a distinct type of dynamical continuation of the static metric. imposing an asymptotic late-time divergence in form of a fractional power-law scaling, tunable to be arbitrarily mild within the considered approximation and effectively taming mass inflation, allows us to single out a family of generalised fan-wang regular black holes.

title: final state of superradiant instability in einstein-maxwell-dilaton black hole
abstract: this article examines the instability of charged black holes, using einstein-maxwell-dilaton theory and a massless charged scalar field. our study demonstrates that these black holes become unstable in a certain range of frequencies, which causes scalar "hair" to form outside the event horizon. by using numerical integration on the coupled field equations, we show that there is a phase transition between a purely charged black hole and a hairy black hole configuration. the results show that the hairy phase appears when the temperature is less than $t_c$, the critical temperature, whereas for $t>t_c$, the system stays purely charged. also, our findings show that the critical temperature increases with the size of the black hole, implying that the onset of the phase transition becomes progressively more difficult for larger horizons. lastly, we see that the system enters a stable equilibrium at the critical temperature, which is the final state of the superradiant instability. these results provide us with useful information on how nonlinear superradiant events change and how scalarized black holes arise in more comprehensive theories of gravity.

title: scalar radiation from circular orbits in d3 brane spacetimes: a mano-suzuki-takasugi-like approach
abstract: we study scalar perturbations in a ten-dimensional d3 brane spacetime, developing a (higher-dimensional) mano-suzuki-takasugi-like formalism adapted to the present case leading to a sourced modification of a mathieu equation. as an application, we compute the energy loss both at infinity and at the horizon in terms of scalar waves due to a scalar charge moving along a circular "equatorial" geodesic.

title: a unified ai framework for rapid and accurate waveform generation of compact binary coalescences
abstract: the astrophysical discovery potential of future gravitational wave detectors will hinge on accurate and rapid waveform generation. third generation detectors are expected to observe many long duration compact binary coalescence signals that can probe binary formation and evolution as well as the nature of matter under extreme conditions. we develop a unified framework that combines physical modeling with deep learning. the framework uses an analytic residual spectral representation, shared learning, and decoders for each binary type. it generates waveforms for binary black holes, binary neutron stars, and neutron star black hole binaries, providing a single unified generator for all compact binary coalescences. the generated waveforms include the physical effects described by each reference model, such as spin precession, higher order modes, matter effects, and postmerger radiation for binary neutron stars. the waveforms span hundreds to thousands of cycles, with mean mismatches ranging from $5.89\times10^{-4}$ to $5.34\times10^{-2}$ relative to the reference waveforms. batch generation achieves a maximum speedup of about 1800 over reference waveform generation.

title: crossover from schwarzian dynamics to rotational soft modes in near-extremal lovelock black holes
abstract: near-extremal black holes are controlled by a small set of soft modes, and counting these modes fixes the coefficient of $\log t$ in the entropy. we ask whether genuine six-derivative interactions change that count, working in seven-dimensional third-order lovelock gravity, the simplest setting where the cubic lovelock term is dynamical. the multiplicities stay the same, but the naive count fails. at fixed charge the maxwell mode is frozen out, and the fifteen rotational modes of the $s^5$ act as a quantum rotor that only switches on above the scale $k_j^{-1}$. as a result, the coefficient of $\log t$ runs from $3/2$ at the lowest temperatures to $9$ above that scale, and never reaches the naive gaussian value $19/2$. we compute the moment of inertia $k_j$ from the charged slow-rotation solution and find that the lovelock couplings move the crossover without changing the multiplicities. only large ads black holes have a wide window in which the full rotational contribution competes with the classical entropy. adding a probe charged scalar, we derive an analytic near-horizon schwinger threshold in the cubic coupling. its large-ads limit tells us when the broad rotational crossover window can coexist with the absence of a charged-scalar breitenlohner--freedman (bf) bound violation.

title: particle dynamics in rotating charged bumblebee black holes: an analytical correspondence with kerr-newman
abstract: in this paper, we establish an analytical correspondence between the equatorial dynamics of spinless and spinning test particles in a slowly rotating charged einstein--bumblebee black hole spacetime and those in an effective kerr--newman spacetime. for spinning particles, the correspondence is established within the mathisson--papapetrou--dixon framework under appropriate parameter matching. we show that corresponding circular orbits have identical radii and coordinate angular velocities, while their radial dynamics and local instability rates exhibit a lorentz-violation-dependent scaling. nevertheless, the correspondence does not imply complete dynamical equivalence, as orbital trajectories and radial perturbation growth over an azimuthal period generally differ. these results delineate the scope and limitations of the effective kerr--newman correspondence by distinguishing the dynamical properties preserved under parameter matching from those modified by the lorentz-violating radial deformation.

title: on the motion of a point electric charge in the field of wu-yang monopoles in bertotti-robinson spacetimes
